role_title: Frontier Data Lead, Code + RL Environments
role_summary: Hands-on frontier technical lead who translates AI lab needs into datasets, RL environments, evals, and proof-of-value loops for coding agents and long-horizon tool-use workflows. Runs the project end to end: scoping with frontier researchers, designing tasks and verifiers, building validation and automation systems, and hiring or leading the engineers, researchers, QAs, and domain experts required to deliver at quality and scale. The hard bar is not generic applied AI or people management; it is post-training and evaluation depth plus enough systems and operational leadership to run a startup-like frontier data project.
geography: San Francisco Bay Area, California, United States
instructions: Treat this as a merged brief, not two independent reqs. Strong candidates may anchor in either coding-agent or RL-environment work, but they must still look capable of leading the full project lifecycle across environments, evals, quality systems, and delivery execution.

Do not over-index on exact titles like Frontier Data Lead. Adjacent titles such as Research Engineer, Applied Scientist, Staff ML Engineer, Principal Engineer, Technical Lead, Engineering Manager who still codes, and Founding Engineer can all be right if the underlying work is right.

The evaluation bar is post-training, environment, or benchmark depth plus systems and team/process leadership. Generic AI app builders, pure copilots, or customer-facing AI delivery profiles without model-improvement or environment-design work should not be rescued by pedigree alone.

Code-lane candidates should show more than using coding models. Look for coding-agent benchmarks, repo sandboxing, patch or test verification, SWE eval harnesses, unit-test generation, task generation, or proof-of-value model improvement on software-engineering tasks.

RL-lane candidates should show more than classical RL familiarity. Look for environment design, reward or verifier design, task realism, trajectory scoring, fine-tuning or post-training loops, or long-horizon eval systems for LLM agents.
Agent infrastructure builders can fit when they built browser-use, computer-use, MCP, tool-calling, or enterprise app simulation environments with clear evaluation and quality methodology.
Strong customer or lab communication is a confidence booster only after the build evidence is real. Sales enablement, solutioning, or stakeholder polish without technical authorship is not enough.
Because this search is Bay Area-specific, local candidates and people already tied to the San Francisco or Peninsula market should be prioritized over remote candidates with no local signal.

For GitHub, prioritize repos showing environments, verifiers, simulators, repo sandboxes, agent-task generation, evaluation harnesses, reward logic, validation tooling, and internal platform code. De-emphasize toy demos, prompt collections, and thin wrappers over hosted APIs.
search_priorities: Staff or principal research engineers, applied scientists, and ML engineers who built coding-agent benchmarks, SWE eval harnesses, repo sandboxes, or software-engineering post-training systems
RL and post-training builders who designed environments, verifiers, reward systems, trajectory scoring, or long-horizon evaluation tasks for LLM agents
Agent-infrastructure builders who created browser-use, computer-use, MCP, function-calling, or enterprise workflow environments with strong validation and observability
Hands-on technical leads or engineering managers who still coded while owning team build-out, QA process design, and direct collaboration with frontier lab researchers or high-end AI customers
Strong Bay Area academic or industry researchers with relevant RL, program synthesis, agent evaluation, or tool-use systems depth who also show practical engineering and delivery instincts
Canonical app-layer GenAI builders only when there is explicit evidence they moved below the application layer into evaluation, data quality, environment design, or model-improvement work
intake_notes: This brief merges two Bay Area Turing roles posted on March 9, 2026: Frontier Data Lead, Code - US and Frontier Data Lead, RL Gyms - US. The shared job is a hands-on frontier technical lead who owns datasets, environments, evals, quality systems, and team/process execution for AI lab customers. The merged interpretation should not require perfectly symmetrical depth in both lanes. Instead, the save bar is: strong anchor in either coding-agent or RL-environment/post-training work, plus enough adjacent fluency to credibly run the full project lifecycle, plus hands-on leadership and systems judgment. Engineering management experience matters, but this is not a manager-only search.

capability_areas.name: 1. RL Environment Design, Verifiers & Post-Training Systems (HARD GATE)
capability_areas.description: Designs or builds the environments, tasks, reward or verifier logic, and post-training loops used to evaluate or improve frontier models. This is the closest work to the RL Gyms half of the role and one of the clearest direct-fit anchors.
builder_signals: Designed RL or agent environments, simulators, tasks, or stateful workflows for model evaluation or improvement
Built reward models, verifier systems, trajectory scoring, or automated success criteria for long-horizon agent behavior
Ran or supported RLHF, DPO, GRPO, PPO, or other post-training and fine-tuning loops tied to measurable model improvement
Created seed data, schemas, APIs, or interaction surfaces that made the environment realistic and useful for post-training
Can describe how environment or reward design changed model behavior, benchmark outcomes, or proof-of-value results
user_signals: Mentioned RL only as a skill keyword or course topic with no evidence of environment or post-training work
Consumed already-tuned models without participating in reward design, task design, or evaluation methodology
Did classical RL experiments in isolation with no visible connection to LLM agents, evaluation systems, or real workflow environments
Managed preference-labeling or annotation operations without designing the methodology

capability_areas.name: 2. Coding Agents, SWE Benchmarks & Repository Evaluation
capability_areas.description: Builds datasets, benchmarks, eval harnesses, or environments for models that write, debug, test, or reason over code. This is the Code half of the role and the other primary direct-fit anchor.
builder_signals: Built or improved coding agents that operate on real repositories or software-development tasks
Created code benchmarks, task suites, or automated verification systems for bug fixing, patch generation, test generation, or repo navigation
Built repo sandboxing, code execution, unit-test generation, or patch-evaluation infrastructure
Generated synthetic code tasks or designed data pipelines that improved coding-model performance
Analyzed model strengths and failure modes on software-engineering tasks and used that analysis to improve the system or benchmark
user_signals: Used Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or other coding tools without building benchmarks, evals, or improvement loops around them
Built standard CI or devtools infrastructure with no model-evaluation or code-generation component
Created generic codegen demos or wrappers without task realism, verification, or dataset methodology

capability_areas.name: 3. Tool-Use Agent Environments: Browser-Use, MCP & Workflow Simulation
capability_areas.description: Builds the interfaces and environments that let agents operate across browsers, tools, APIs, and realistic enterprise workflows. This captures the overlap between coding agents and RL gyms around long-horizon, multi-step agent behavior.
builder_signals: Designed browser-use or computer-use tasks, simulators, or environments for agent evaluation
Built MCP, function-calling, tool-use, or API surfaces that agents used to complete realistic tasks
Modeled databases, schemas, and interfaces for simulated business or consumer applications
Built state management, trajectory capture, observability, or validation for multi-step agent workflows
Integrated agents with enterprise or consumer tools in ways that preserved realism, difficulty, and measurable outcomes
user_signals: Built simple chatbots or RAG apps without multi-step tool use or environment complexity
Used pre-built agent frameworks without owning the environment, interface, or evaluation design
Did browser automation or QA scripting unrelated to LLM agents or evaluation systems

capability_areas.name: 4. Data Quality, Task Generation & Evaluation Operations
capability_areas.description: Designs the quality systems that make environments and datasets usable at frontier standards: realism, difficulty, correctness, diversity, validation, and human review. This is the day-to-day operating core of the role.
builder_signals: Defined quality rubrics, review criteria, or annotation methodology for datasets, tasks, or environment outputs
Built automated validation scripts, evaluation pipelines, or regression checks for data and task quality
Created synthetic data or task generation systems that increased coverage, realism, or difficulty
Designed human-in-the-loop review processes with measurable quality standards
Improved environment or dataset quality through explicit work on correctness, diversity, realism, or failure-mode coverage
user_signals: Managed data operations or QA throughput without designing the technical quality system
Did general ETL, analytics, or reporting work with no connection to model evaluation or training quality
Performed annotation or review work using someone else's rubric without creating the methodology

capability_areas.name: 5. Systems Architecture, Sandboxing & Internal Tooling
capability_areas.description: Builds the surrounding systems that make these projects operational at scale: internal tools, APIs, dashboards, sandboxes, databases, queues, and automation. The role needs more than ML intuition; it needs strong technical systems judgment.
builder_signals: Built internal tools for data generation, verification, sandboxing, scraping, or evaluation operations
Designed APIs, databases, worker systems, or task queues that supported environment or post-training pipelines
Made architecture tradeoffs around throughput, isolation, correctness, observability, latency, or cost
Built dashboards or reporting APIs for customers or internal teams to inspect model or environment performance
Shows fluency in Python and enough systems or full-stack engineering to ship production-grade tooling
user_signals: Worked on pure infrastructure or platform systems with no visible link to agents, post-training, environments, or evaluation
Built frontend shells or dashboards without owning the data pipeline or backend system
Did data engineering for analytics without any model-improvement or evaluation awareness

capability_areas.name: 6. Hands-On Technical Leadership, Team Building & Lab-Facing Delivery
capability_areas.description: Leads the project like a startup while still contributing technically: hiring the right team, setting QA processes, translating client needs into specs, and driving high-stakes execution across multiple stakeholders.
builder_signals: Led engineers, researchers, QAs, or domain experts while still writing code or directly shaping technical decisions
Translated frontier lab or demanding customer asks into environment specs, milestones, and technical execution plans
Interviewed, hired, onboarded, trained, or mentored technical contributors for specialized data or environment projects
Owned delivery risk across quality, throughput, scope, and stakeholder communication for complex technical programs
Produced eval reports, technical writeups, or benchmark narratives that informed roadmap or customer conversations
user_signals: Pure people manager or org leader who no longer appears to build or make close technical decisions
Pre-sales, solutions, or product leader whose work centers on communication rather than technical authorship
Research manager or program manager coordinating technical work without personal implementation depth

depth_distinction.builder_definition: A builder for this role personally designs and shapes the technical system: the environment, task logic, verifier or reward logic, evaluation methodology, data-quality process, or surrounding tooling. They do not merely consume coding models or talk about agents at a high level. They can explain how a frontier lab ask turns into a concrete environment or benchmark spec, what makes the tasks realistic and difficult, how quality is enforced, and what systems are required to deliver and iterate at scale. They may manage people, but they still operate close enough to the code and design to make the key calls themselves.
depth_distinction.user_definition: A user or adjacent profile works with AI products, copilots, or teams using these systems without directly designing the environment, evaluation, or improvement loop. This includes generic app-layer AI builders, solutioning or pre-sales roles, infrastructure teams that serve models without touching training or evaluation methodology, annotation operators following pre-written rubrics, and managers who coordinate the work but no longer shape the technical system in detail.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: CODING-AGENT SPECIALISTS: Strong fit even without explicit RL titles if they built real SWE benchmarks, repo sandboxes, automated verification, task generation, or post-training loops tied to coding-model improvement. RL / POST-TRAINING SPECIALISTS: Strong fit even without coding-agent titles if they designed environments, verifiers, reward systems, schemas, APIs, and proof-of-value loops for LLM agents in realistic workflows. AGENT INFRASTRUCTURE BUILDERS: Browser-use, MCP, or workflow-environment builders can fit when they also show quality systems and model-evaluation rigor. MANAGEMENT: Formal management experience helps because the role requires hiring and QA process design, but pure managers without recent technical depth should not pass. BAY AREA ACADEMICS: Postdocs or researchers can fit if their work clearly crosses into implementable environments, benchmarks, or tooling rather than staying purely theoretical.

inferential_save_rules.description: This market includes frontier-lab and Bay Area startup profiles with sparse public detail. When a profile has a strong prior of fit but insufficient bullet-level evidence, prefer INFERENTIAL_SAVE over silent rejection so the recruiter can review it.
conditions: Current technical role at a frontier AI lab or elite coding-agent company with title or team context suggesting post-training, evals, code generation, agents, or research engineering, even if bullets are sparse
PhD or strong research profile in RL, program synthesis, agents, or LLM evaluation with a current hands-on engineering or research-engineering role and limited LinkedIn detail
Staff or principal engineer at a strong AI company whose visible profile shows agent, benchmark, or environment adjacency but not enough detail to prove direct ownership
inferential_save_rules.note: Use this pathway for strong priors that still need recruiter confirmation, not for weak maybes.

non_fit_patterns.label: Generic GenAI application builders
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers or FDE-style profiles who shipped copilots, chat workflows, or agent apps for end users but did not work on post-training, environment design, benchmark design, verifier logic, or evaluation methodology.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: They are building on top of models rather than improving models through data, environments, or evaluation systems. The role sits below the application layer.
examples: Enterprise copilot builder using APIs and RAG only
Forward deployed engineer shipping AI workflows with no benchmark or model-improvement work

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure devtools or SWE infrastructure
non_fit_patterns.description: Strong software engineers building developer tools, CI, code review systems, or repository infrastructure with no visible AI, evaluation, or post-training component.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The code domain is relevant, but the model-improvement and environment-design layer is missing.
examples: Staff devtools engineer building CI platforms
Infrastructure engineer for repo management with no AI evaluation work

non_fit_patterns.label: MLOps, model serving, or platform-only ML infrastructure
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers who deploy, monitor, or scale models in production but do not design training data, benchmarks, environments, or evaluation systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: They operate around the model rather than shaping the post-training and quality loop that this role owns.
examples: MLOps engineer managing model inference platforms
ML platform engineer building feature stores or serving infrastructure

non_fit_patterns.label: Annotation or data-ops execution without methodology design
non_fit_patterns.description: People who label data, review outputs, or manage annotation operations without creating the quality rubric, validation tooling, or evaluation system.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: This role designs the process and the technical quality bar; it is not an annotation-operations role.
examples: Data-ops lead focused on throughput and reviewer staffing

non_fit_patterns.label: Classical RL or robotics research without LLM-agent bridge
non_fit_patterns.description: Researchers who worked on control, robotics, or simulation environments but show no evidence of LLM agents, tool use, code tasks, post-training data, or scalable evaluation systems.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Some of the skills are adjacent, but the direct connection to frontier model improvement for coding and tool-use agents is missing.
examples: Robotics RL researcher with no LLM or evaluation-system work
Control-theory simulation expert with no agent or post-training bridge

non_fit_patterns.label: Manager, PM, or solutions leader without recent technical authorship
non_fit_patterns.description: Leads organizations or customer conversations around AI work but no longer appears to design environments, write code, or own evaluation methodology personally.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The role requires hands-on technical leadership, not managerial oversight alone.
examples: Engineering director who manages research teams but has no recent technical contribution evidence
Solutions or product leader for AI platforms without direct build ownership

non_fit_override_rule: A non-fit pattern is overridden when the profile shows concrete builder-level evidence in a capability area. For example, a devtools engineer who built coding-agent benchmarks or a robotics researcher who later designed LLM tool-use environments should be evaluated on the actual evidence, not the default lookalike label.

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Any technical role touching post-training, evals, agents, data, research engineering, or model-improvement systems is a strong signal. Pure infra-only or manager-only profiles still need adjacent evidence.
Strong signal when the candidate worked on agents, benchmarks, evals, repo workflows, code intelligence, or model-improvement loops. Generic product, GTM, or unrelated platform roles are not enough.

Need at least one visible sign of environment, benchmark, evaluation, data-quality, or post-training depth. Company signal alone is helpful but not decisive because these employers also have adjacent roles.
Need publications, open-source work, or project detail showing RL, agents, program synthesis, LLM evaluation, or systems work that plausibly transfers into implementable environments and benchmarks.
Evaluate based on actual capability-area evidence, depth, and Bay Area fit rather than employer name.

minimum_bar_description: 7+ years of total hands-on engineering, ML, or research-engineering experience, with clear evidence that the candidate still operates close to the technical system. Save anyone who shows direct depth in either coding-agent or RL-environment and post-training work, plus enough systems and delivery leadership to run a frontier data project end to end. They do not need identical tenure in both lanes, but they should have a clear anchor in one and credible adjacent evidence in the other. Strong frontier-lab, Bay Area startup, or research signals should raise tolerance for sparse bullets when the underlying trajectory suggests real post-training or evaluation depth.

post_save_modifiers.name: Frontier Lab / High-Trust Customer Credibility
post_save_modifiers.trigger: Candidate already qualifies as a SAVE, SIGNAL_SAVE, TRANSFERABLE_SAVE, or INFERENTIAL_SAVE based on the core capability areas
post_save_modifiers.if_present: Boost confidence by 0.05-0.1. Note that the candidate appears credible with frontier researchers or similarly demanding technical customers.
post_save_modifiers.if_absent: No adjustment. Lack of explicit customer-facing evidence is not a rejection reason if the technical bar is clearly met.
signals: Direct collaboration with frontier lab researchers or elite technical customers
Owned technical progress reviews, evaluation reports, or solutioning conversations on high-stakes AI work
Acts as a trusted technical lead rather than a narrow individual contributor only

post_save_modifiers.name: Public Technical Authority
post_save_modifiers.trigger: Candidate already qualifies as a SAVE, SIGNAL_SAVE, TRANSFERABLE_SAVE, or INFERENTIAL_SAVE based on the core capability areas
post_save_modifiers.if_present: Boost confidence by 0.03-0.08. Note that public open-source work, papers, or technical writing increases confidence in depth and signal clarity.
post_save_modifiers.if_absent: No adjustment. Do not penalize candidates whose best work is private.
signals: Open-source repos or contributions tied to environments, evals, post-training, or coding agents
Research papers or technical posts on RL environments, benchmarks, program synthesis, or agent evaluation
Public benchmark reports, demo systems, or technical writeups that show unusual depth

notes: Created on April 8, 2026 by merging Turing roles 5822272004 (Frontier Data Lead, Code - US) and 5822287004 (Frontier Data Lead, RL Gyms - US) into one Bay Area search brief. Core thesis: save strong anchor-in-one-lane builders who can credibly span the broader frontier data project, rather than requiring perfect symmetry across both code and RL environments.
